newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares rise sharply, Bezeq surges.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares rise sharply, Bezeq surges.

text.p: Israeli shares surged across the board on Tuesday on hopes of an agreement for an Israeli troop redeployment in the West Bank town of Hebron, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares gained 2.53 percent, or 4.53 points, to 183.23 on low turnover of 59 million shekels against 60 million on Monday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index rose 3.10 percent to 193.40.
"The mood in the market has suddenly improved. Maybe its because there is a feeling that an agreement on Hebron can be reached soon," said Irit Ben-Zur at Sahar Securities.
Israel and the Palestinian Authority began talks last week on implementing a deal to redeploy Israeli troops in Hebron signed by Israel's previous government.

"The fact that (Prime Minister Benjamin) Netanyahu called for an interest rate cut is also positive. The Bank of Israel will not lower the rate but at least we know Netanyahu's position," Ben-Zur said.
At a meeting with business leaders and government officials on Monday Netanyahu asked the Bank of Israel Governor Jacob Frenkel to cut the interest rate.

Bezeq Israel Telecom, the second most active share, surged 5.5 percent to 774. Bezeq's board of directors approved on Tuesday a plan for the reduction of the company's workforce by 1,050 employees within five years.

Makhteshim Chemical Works rose 3.5 percent to 1,779. Makhteshim's subsidiary Agan Chemicals Manufacturers gained 2.75 percent to 5,030. Both companies were rated a "buy" by Societe Generale Strauss Turnbull.

"The redeployment of Israeli troops in Hebron will apparently take place soon. Investors are also hoping for a very low consumer price index (CPI) for September," said a trader at United Mizrahi Bank.
The CPI, released after the end of the trading day, rose 0.4 percent in September against a similar rise of 0.4 percent in August.

"The figure is expected to be relatively low. The Bank of Israel will leave the interest rate unchanged but a low CPI is still a very good sign. The market also rose today because of the high activity of Maof options speculators," she said.
The most active share was Koor Industries, which jumped 4.0 percent to 27,667 on volume of 5.5 million shekels.
Bank Hapoalim, surged 4.5 percent to 448 on turnover of 2.6 million shekels.
